questions.title: Identify Mutually Exclusive Pairs - decide for each pair of events whether they can happen together, which is the whole definition before any arithmetic
Mutual Exclusivity from a Two-Way Table - read the joint and union probabilities off a genre table, then decide whether the two events are mutually exclusive
Multiplication Rule for Independent Events - P(A and B), P(A or B) and P(neither) when independence lets the two probabilities simply multiply
Full Two-Way Workup Ending in an Independence Test - marginal, joint and conditional probabilities from a commute table, then compare the product against the joint to test independence
Dependence via a Reduced Sample Space - the size of the space once the first birth is known, and the conditional probability of two boys on it
Why the Naive Sum Fails on Overlapping Events - chain the naive sum, the addition rule and the complement to reach P(neither), and see where the first one goes wrong
Conditional Probability from the Formula - apply P(A given B) = P(A and B) / P(B), the quantity the independence test compares against

Pre-FRQ Grade an Independence Check - the scenario and grading checklist of a mutually-exclusive-versus-independent question, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
